problem: The line 'More resistance removes more energy per ampere' is loose. For a fixed I₀ the stored energy ½LI₀² is the same whatever R is; R only changes how fast that energy leaves.
fix: For RL, at any instant the power dissipated is i²R, so a larger R burns the same initial ½LI₀² in a shorter time. That is why τ = L/R falls as R rises.

problem: 'That is the charging curve' is imprecise. On a charging curve the value at t = τ is 63.2 % of the final value, not of the starting value.
fix: Writing 63.2 % mistakes the charging curve, where the value reaches 63.2 % of its final value at t = τ, for the source-free decay, which falls to 36.8 % of its starting value.

problem: The tangent series is defined as 1 − x and is tabulated all the way to −4, while the plot's y minimum is 0. The line will be clipped or will stretch the y-axis far below zero, and the tangent only matters between t = 0 and t = τ.
fix: Tabulate the tangent only for 0 ≤ t/τ ≤ 1 (from (0, 1) to (1, 0)), or set the y minimum to about −0.5.

problem: 'one unit on the x-axis is 5 ms' is unclear because the x-axis is labelled t/τ, not t.
fix: Say: in the worked example τ = 5 ms, so one unit of t/τ corresponds to 5 ms of real time.

problem: A fan slowing down is mostly mechanical inertia, not an electrical time constant. A student may connect the two wrongly.
fix: Use electrical examples: a capacitor-run lamp fading after switch-off, an LED dimming as its supply capacitor drains, a relay coil's current collapsing.
